quality_notes: The Government Printer PDF is a 4-page scan with no text layer, so this tree is parsed from an offline OCR reading. Wording has not been proof-read against the scan.

This is a 1958 Government Press print. The OCR reads its quotation marks as letter pairs throughout -- an opening quote as '<c', '<6', 'c6', 'cc' or 'c<' and a closing quote as '>>', '3>', '>.' or ',9'. Every quoted extract in the body is affected. The wording between the marks is generally sound; the marks themselves are not.
Marginal notes and the provision interleave in this print, so several section headings carry fragments of the note's column out of order. See known_ocr_defects.

Running headers and the printer's imprint fall inside section 2's text ('1-J N. R 21 670-2 775 (2/5S) 4 Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 1958'). They are page furniture, not part of the provision.
